area_summary: The 3D side has two narrow choke points, and almost everything follows from them. (1) preparation() at 0x8017BE20 runs every frame at the top of camera_execute. It writes view->mAspect (store 0x8017BE88) = the 4/3 literal at 0x803FA998 × g_HIO.mAspectRatio (0x803B9A08, 0.96). That one value drives camera_draw's C_MTXPerspective (0x8017C444) and view_setup's clipper (0x8017BF90). It also drives mProjViewMtx (cMtx_concatProjView, d_camera.cpp:5492), which mDoLib_project and every screen-space check use, and the JPA particle aspect (mDoGph_Painter 0x8000B200 and 0x8000B4F8 → C_MTXLightPerspective 0x8025FC14 and 0x8025FCD8). (2) mDoLib_project returns EFB pixels (0..640 across the viewport). Under the anamorphic model, EFB pixels are exactly the full, stretched screen. So every check that compares a projected point with 0..640 / 0..480 / the scissor, or samples peekZ or GXPeekARGB there, becomes correct by itself once the aspect is widened. That covers sun visibility, clouds, fireflies, lantern, pointInSight, blur centre and the picto-box area calculation, and it removes the wrong-pixel peekZ problem the Dolphin hack has. What does not follow: (a) distance-from-centre maths in EFB pixels (lens-flare angle, sun falloff, moon/star exclusion, telescope look-in radius, npc_ls1's telescope) becomes anisotropic by F. All of it is cosmetic or a small leniency. (b) Things drawn in 2D at a projected point (sights, enemy HP bar, text anchors, baton sparkle, our name tags) land at EFB x, so they drift toward the centre if the 2D pass is globally compressed. (c) Fixed EFB rectangles: the picto-box judge rectangle and the photo capture. All are DOL `bl mDoLib_project` sites, so one shared C wrapper ws_project_2d (x' = 320 + (x-320)·F in mode 2, identity otherwise) applied with hook_branchlink fixes (a) and (b) cheaply. Every site needs its own hook, but the code is shared. Each screen-space check's sense was verified by reading its function in the decomp. Knob verdict: section 9 of the culling plan is right that g_HIO.mAspectRatio is never written at runtime. Its only store is the ctor at 0x800230CC, called from __sinit_f_ap_game_cpp at 0x800232E4, and no decomp REL references it. But its six readers include three that must NOT widen: the stage-transition fade that warps a full-screen capture (dOvlpFd2) and the two menu cloth backdrops. The 4/3 literal 0x803FA998 has exactly one reader (preparation 0x8017BE5C) and is a plain data word. It is the cheap, exact knob for mode 2, and Dolphin's own Gecko code uses the same word. Lock-on framing (mWindowAspectRatio) should stay 4:3. Cheap: the knob (one data write), the automatic followers, the wrapper. Expensive: the picto box (EFB rectangles, photo capture size), and REL-only sites (npc_ls1, our name tags).

items.fix: Boot-time and op-time data write from C, no code patch. In ws_init and in the WWAP_OP_WS_SET handler: mode 2 → *(f32*)0x803FA998 = (4.0f/3.0f)*factor; any other mode → write back 0x3FAAAAAB bit-exactly. Values: 16:9 0x3FE38E39, 16:10 0x3FCCCCCD, 21:9 (factor 1.7778) 0x4017B426, 32:9 0x40638E39. Safe at main01_init: .sdata2 is DOL-loaded and nothing else writes it; a hot reset reloads the DOL and runs main01_init again. It takes effect on the next camera_execute. Everything else in this list that says 'follows' then follows: projection, clipper (ws_clip_aspect passes through in mode 2), mProjViewMtx, mDoLib_project, JPA. Leaves alone, on purpose: the fade capture warp, both cloth backdrops, the file-select camera (see their items). One known side effect: init_phase2 (0x8017C928) stores an unwidened 1.28 for the first frame after camera creation (stage load, under the fade). Harmless.
